title: Squeeze a spring collar open and slide it past the sleeve shoulder flush against the outer weight plate
instruction: Seat the spring collar past the sleeve shoulder flush against the outer plate clamped onto the barbell sleeve without shifting the bar, and clear both grippers.
context: Every home gym workout and daily barbell strength session uses spring clip collars to lock weight plates against the sleeve flange so plates cannot rattle or slide off during lifts. Because the crossed spring clamp shoes catch behind the 58 mm sleeve shoulder unless squeezed open and the axial seating push against the outer plate slides an unbraced 780 g bar forward along its low-friction cradle, stabilizing the bar while squeezing and sliding the collar seats it cleanly.
setup: A fixed steel benchtop barbell cradle stand (310 x 240 mm footprint on 3 mm rubber corner feet) sits anchored at (0.295, -0.025) m on the station tabletop with two low-friction channel stanchions 282 mm apart supporting the sleeve centerline 76 mm above the tabletop. An unbolted 780 g loadable barbell sleeve assembly rests level at (0.295, -0.025) m along world X: a 50 mm chrome loading sleeve (128 mm long, with 26 mm top and bottom anti-rotation flats) carrying a 58 mm retention shoulder lug ring (8 mm wide) at x = 0.227 m, two rubber-coated fractional weight plates (118 mm and 134 mm outer diameters, 15 mm thick each, outer hub face at x = 0.285 m) against a 72 mm inner flange, a 28 mm rear journal shaft, and a radial 28 mm knurled stabilizer handle extending 160 mm along +Y to (0.330, 0.135) m. A 320 g three-turn chrome spring clip collar (250 g coil body with 50 mm concentric guide skids plus two 35 g crossed spring-wire stirrup jaws) starts pre-mounted on the outer 50 mm sleeve pilot at x = 0.187 m; at rest its side shoes embrace the sleeve and block against the 58 mm shoulder, while pinching its two vertical red vinyl handles (42 mm above the sleeve axis) across an 8 mm stroke against 35 N spring preload (2200 N/m per leg) opens the clamp shoes to 63 mm span. One fixed starting layout; arms start at ready pose.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial from physical end-state geometry with a caliper, ruler, and digital protractor; the run succeeds once 1.0 holds continuously for 3 s. Possible scores 0.0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.0. 1.0: the barbell stays seated within 12 mm horizontally and 8 mm vertically of its stand cradle and tilted at most 6 deg, the collar stays coaxial within 10 mm and 12 deg of the sleeve, the collar rests past the sleeve shoulder flush within 8 mm of the outer plate hub, both spring jaws are clamped within 4 mm on the sleeve, and both grippers are more than 120 mm clear of the collar, barbell sleeve, and radial stabilizer handle. 0.75: collar flush within 8 mm of the outer plate past the shoulder and clamped within 4 mm with the bar in its cradle, gripper within 120 mm. 0.50: collar flush within 8 mm of the outer plate past the shoulder with the bar in its cradle, spring jaws not clamped within 4 mm. 0.25: barbell seated and collar coaxial and slid at least 30 mm inward along the sleeve, not yet flush within 8 mm of the outer plate past the shoulder. 0.0: otherwise (doing nothing, unsqueezed push blocked behind the 58 mm shoulder, off-axis drop, or unbraced bar shifted past 12 mm).
reset_notes: Seat the 780 g barbell sleeve assembly level on the two stand saddles at (0.295, -0.025) m with the outer plate hub at x = 0.285 m, squeeze the 320 g spring collar open, slide it back outside the 58 mm shoulder to the outer pilot at x = 0.187 m, and release so its jaws clamp the pilot.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (20 Hz control). The three-turn spring collar uses an 8-sided hollow coil barrel with 50 mm concentric guide bushings and two crossed prismatic spring-wire stirrup jaws (2200 N/m per leg, non-overlapping handles) rather than continuous helical wire torsion; the barbell uses rigid primitive cylinders, key flats, and anti-roll lands. Friction and contact softness are calibrated within 0.8x to 1.5x margin.
